scripts.name: start 5477
scripts.command:
boo kill t3-worktree-5477 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; for attempt in $(seq 1 40); do ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ':5477 ' || break; sleep 0.25; done; boo new t3-worktree-5477 -d -- bash -lc '
cd /home/ylapin.guest/.t3/worktrees/t3code/t3code-84ecd53d
export T3CODE_HOME=/home/ylapin.guest/.t3/dev
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/home/ylapin.guest/.portless/ca.pem
export PORT=5477
export T3CODE_PORT=13777
export VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:5477
# This owns the whole stack: web on 5477 and the backend on 13777. Never start
# either one separately -- a second backend either fails with EADDRINUSE on
# 13777 or, worse, comes up on another port against a different state.sqlite.
# Deliberately no VITE_HTTP_URL/VITE_WS_URL: those get baked into the bundle and
# would send a phone to its own localhost:13777. Unset, the client targets its
# own origin and Vite proxies /api and /ws to T3CODE_PORT.
unset PORTLESS_URL PORTLESS_TAILSCALE PORTLESS_TAILSCALE_URL PORTLESS_LAN
vp run --filter=@t3tools/contracts --filter=@t3tools/web --filter=t3 --parallel dev &
runner=$!
for attempt in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:13777/.well-known/t3/environment >/dev/null; then
    echo "T3 backend ready on 13777"
    # A fixed tailnet port is reused on every start, so the phone URL never
    # changes and no stale `tailscale serve` entries pile up.
    tailscale serve --bg --yes --https=8477 http://127.0.0.1:5477 >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "could not pin tailscale serve on 8477" >&2
    echo "phone: https://lima-default.tail052173.ts.net:8477"
    wait "$runner"
    exit $?
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$runner" 2>/dev/null; then
    wait "$runner"
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
done
echo "T3 backend did not become ready on 13777" >&2
kill "$runner" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$runner"
exit 1
'
